description: Portfolio defaults for pull request volume. A consumer overrides any of these by setting the same key in its own renovate.json.

prConcurrentLimit caps the open Renovate pull requests at 5. Where branch protection runs with strict: true, every merge re-queues the full workflow fan-out of every open branch -- fewer open branches is the lever (nolte/gh-plumbing#439, measurement in nolte/claude-shared#644).
Lowering prConcurrentLimit never closes an already-open pull request. The new cap takes effect as the open ones merge or close.
prHourlyLimit: 2 restates Renovate's own default and is set explicitly to document the intent.
Vulnerability alerts skip the line: their pull requests ignore these limits and are never grouped, so a security fix is never held back.

packageRules.description: Pin GitHub Actions to full-length commit digests. A tag is mutable even from a trusted publisher (CVE-2025-30066), so a digest is the only immutable action reference; pinDigests also makes each pin age as a reviewable pull request instead of silently.

Group the GitHub Actions digest bumps into one pull request. An action digest bump carries no individual changelog, so a single grouped pull request loses no review signal and keeps the open pull request budget free for updates that do carry one. The group stays limited to the github-actions manager, the one this preset pins itself: a container image digest rebuild can carry a security fix without a vulnerability alert, so it stays its own pull request. groupSlug is set explicitly because Renovate's own pinDigest default carries the slug pin-dependencies, which would otherwise split the group across the branches renovate/pin-dependencies and renovate/digests. Portfolio default -- a consumer opts out by setting groupName: null and groupSlug: null for the same match in its own renovate.json. Vulnerability alerts are exempt from grouping, so a security fix still arrives as its own pull request.

Keep every nolte/gh-plumbing update out of the digests group and off automerge, whichever manager proposes it: workflow uses: references and preset references alike, hence no matchManagers. spec/project/workflow-health/ (nolte/claude-shared) treats each gh-plumbing bump as a candidate that needs its own human acknowledgement, the portfolio-wide rollback signal for a reusable-workflow change, so a pin or digest update must not hide among third-party action digests. This rule must stay after the digests group rule, because a later rule's null resets the group. automerge: false is the preset default only: a consumer's own packageRules are evaluated after this preset and can override it, which the workflow-health spec forbids for gh-plumbing.

Keep every pre-commit pin in lockstep. A repository typically pins the pre-commit package twice: once in a requirements file, read by the pip_requirements manager, and once inline in a workflow run: line, read by the inline pip pin manager below. Two managers propose two pull requests, and merging one leaves the pins apart. One group puts both bumps on a single branch (nolte/gh-plumbing#467). matchDatasources keeps the hook repositories of the pre-commit manager out: those resolve through git tags, not PyPI.

customManagers.description: Age the hacs/action digest. Its comment names a branch rather than a version, because hacs/action's newest tag dates from 2022, and the github-actions manager resolves a comment through the github-tags datasource where a branch name finds nothing. This manager resolves the same line through git-refs instead.

Age the hassfest digest. Its comment names a branch rather than a version, because home-assistant/actions has no usable release tag, and the github-actions manager resolves a comment through the github-tags datasource -- where a branch name finds nothing and no bump is ever proposed. This manager resolves the same line through git-refs instead, so the pin ages like every other one.

Age the PyPI pins a workflow installs inline, for example pip install pytest==9.1.1 in a run: line or an input value. A reusable workflow runs in the consumer's checkout and can't read a requirements file of its own repository, so the pin has to stay inline, where no built-in manager reads it (nolte/gh-plumbing#467). The first expression takes one pip install command up to a shell separator, the second each name==version inside it. Only exact == pins match, so ranges, extras, and -r files stay out. Scoped to .github/workflows. The depType workflow-pip-pin lets a consumer opt out with a packageRules entry that matches it and sets enabled: false.
